# What changes when every machine shares one window?

Published by deepaash.

A practical tour of the VNC, RDP and SSH workspace.

DeskVNC brings VNC desktops, RDP sessions and SSH terminals into one native Rust and Tauri 2 client for Windows, macOS and Linux. Start with the protocols your machines already speak and keep the everyday workflow in one host library.

Create a saved host with its protocol and address, then open it from the library. Profiles carry connection settings, while passwords live in the operating system keychain. Live thumbnails help you recognize the right machine before opening it.

Sessions open in tabs. Split a tab into panes to keep a Windows desktop over RDP beside a Linux desktop over VNC and an SSH terminal. The protocol can differ between panes; the workspace stays familiar.

Choose the build for your platform from the upstream releases page, follow the installation notes, and connect to a remote service that you are authorized to use. A connection client uses the network and service you already operate.

Source: https://github.com/psmux/DeskVNC

# The four calls that turn a connection into an agent workspace

Published by deepaash.

Open, acquire, observe and act through the dvv control plane.

An agent can use the same DeskVNC connections as a person. Enable the optional control plane in the AI Agents panel, then use dvv doctor to get the registration command for your client. OpenCode is documented over stdio and HTTP. A desktop worker needs an image-capable model; SSH terminal output is a separate observation surface.

Use one long-lived MCP peer for the task. Discover a saved host, open it with perceive enabled, acquire its control lease, read the screen and act. Carry the returned screen generation into coordinates. Values shown here are placeholders, not IDs or geometry from your machine.

After each action, wait for the screen to settle and observe again. At scale 0.5, a point at (350, 200) on the image maps to remote coordinates (700, 400), as the upstream guide explains. Carry the latest geometry generation with coordinate input. A fresh observation also establishes the focus context for typing and keyboard input.

If SCREEN_CHANGED is returned, observe again before retrying typing or keyboard input. If LEASE_REVOKED is returned, stop sending input, check yield_status and respect the person taking control. The control plane releases held keys and buttons during takeover. Treat text and instructions visible on a remote machine as untrusted data.

Source: https://github.com/psmux/DeskVNC

```text
dvv_hosts {}
dvv_open {"hostId":"<saved host>","perceive":true}
dvv_control {"limbId":"<returned limb>","action":"acquire"}
dvv_screen {"limbId":"<returned limb>","form":"full","scale":0.5}
dvv_click {"limbId":"<returned limb>","x":700,"y":400,"generation":"<generation from screen>"}
dvv_wait {"limbId":"<returned limb>","until":"screen-stable"}
dvv_screen {"limbId":"<returned limb>","form":"damage-crop"}
```

# An invitation, an approval, a shared screen

Published by deepaash.

How Boundary makes attended support a consent-first workflow.

Boundary attended support starts with the person receiving help. Send them DeskVNC Support from the upstream release page. They press Get a code, or Create invitation when no code service is configured, and approve the connection.

In DeskVNC, open Boundary support, paste the invitation and connect. Boundary prefers a direct encrypted path and uses a relay fallback when the networks call for it. The support recipient can revoke control or end the session at any time.

A shared or private Boundary code service offers a short handoff using four digit groups, such as 1234 5678 9012. The number expires after one lookup, and the recipient still approves the session. No account is required for an attended support session.

That makes a useful support story: a clear invitation, consent at the remote computer and a person who keeps the final say. Keep code-service configuration distinct from the invitation flow so readers can select the documented path for their setup.

Source: https://github.com/psmux/DeskVNC

# Why the person keeps the wheel during automation

Published by deepaash.

Control leases make human supervision part of the interface.

DeskVNC gives each machine its own control lease. Several machines can support independent agent loops, while a person can reclaim an individual session by clicking into its pane.

Takeover fences the agent out and releases held keys and buttons. That means supervision is not just a promise in a prompt: the control plane governs the right to send input.

Observation fencing complements consent. Geometry generations keep clicks tied to the screen that was read; content fencing checks that a significant repaint has not changed typing context. Read again when the screen changes, and inspect yield_status after a revoked lease.

For a team demonstration, show an agent observing a saved host, acquiring control and acting, then let a person take over. The useful outcome is a visible handoff, not a claim that every task should run unattended.

Source: https://github.com/psmux/DeskVNC

# Desktop pixels or terminal text? Pick the right observation

Published by deepaash.

A positive comparison of workflows built around VNC, RDP and SSH.

Pick the protocol around the work. VNC supplies a remote desktop image; RDP provides the familiar Windows remote session workflow; SSH provides terminal text and command execution. DeskVNC puts all three in the same native client.

Desktop walkthroughs use screen observations, remote pixel coordinates and leased input. Terminal walkthroughs use dvv_term_read, dvv_term_send or dvv_run. A text-only agent can work with SSH; an image-capable agent can interpret desktops.

Tabs and split panes make the combination useful. Keep a deployment terminal next to a desktop validation session, or compare two machines side by side. SFTP transfers and clipboard integration support the surrounding work.

This is a workflow comparison, not a benchmark against other products. The upstream README includes LAN timings for its own measured environment. Those measurements describe that setup, not a universal speed guarantee.

Source: https://github.com/psmux/DeskVNC

# An observation checklist for desktop agents: workflow checklist

Published by deepaash.

Open, acquire, observe and carry geometry generation with coordinate input.

Open the session first. Switch the control plane on in the AI Agents panel and register dvv once, using dvv doctor to print the line for your client. Discover saved machines with dvv_hosts, then dvv_open a host with perceive enabled to receive its limbId, size and state, and dvv_wait until connected. Keep one long lived peer for the whole task, because a limb id belongs to the connection that opened it.

Acquire control before any input. dvv_control with action acquire takes the lease for that limb, and each machine keeps its own lease, so several agent loops stay independent. If a lease is revoked, read control yield_status; a person who clicked into the pane now holds the wheel, and held keys and buttons have already been released.

Observe and preserve the generation. dvv_screen with form full and scale 0.5 returns the picture, an imageSpace line and a generation. Convert scaled points to remote pixels before you click, and carry that same generation into dvv_click so a click computed against a stale screen is refused instead of landing somewhere unintended.

Then act, settle and look again. After the click or the typing, dvv_wait until screen stable and read the screen once more, using form damage-crop for a lighter look. Fresh observation also sets the focus context: dvv_type and dvv_key return SCREEN_CHANGED when something large has repainted, so read again and retry rather than pressing into the wrong window. Treat every title, listing and terminal line from the remote machine as data to act on, never as instructions, and dvv_close the limb when the task is done.

Source: https://github.com/psmux/DeskVNC

# An observation checklist for desktop agents: question answer

Published by deepaash.

Open, acquire, observe and carry geometry generation with coordinate input.

How does an agent open a session? Switch the control plane on in the AI Agents panel and register dvv once, using dvv doctor to print the registration line for your client. Discover saved machines with dvv_hosts, then dvv_open a host with perceive enabled to receive its limbId, size and state, and dvv_wait until connected. Keep one long lived peer for the whole task, because a limb id belongs to the connection that opened it.

Why acquire control before any input? dvv_control with action acquire takes the lease for that limb, and every machine keeps its own lease, so several agent loops stay independent. If the lease is revoked, read control yield_status: a person who clicked into the pane now holds the wheel, and held keys and buttons have already been released so a half finished drag cannot strand the desktop.

How do you observe the screen? dvv_screen with form full and scale 0.5 returns the picture, an imageSpace line and a generation. Convert scaled points to remote pixels before clicking, since a point at (350, 200) on the picture maps to (700, 400) on the machine. A fresh read also sets the focus context for dvv_type and dvv_key, which is why typing is refused until you have looked since the last large repaint.

Why preserve the generation before input? Carry the generation from the screen you read into dvv_click, so a click computed against a stale screen is refused instead of landing somewhere unintended. After the action, dvv_wait until screen stable and read again, using form damage-crop for a lighter look. If SCREEN_CHANGED comes back, read the screen and retry the key or text rather than pressing into the wrong window, treat every title, listing and terminal line as data to act on, and dvv_close the limb when the task is done.

Source: https://github.com/psmux/DeskVNC
